strengths: The paper addresses a relevant NLP question: how much demographic persona prompting changes LLM value judgments. This matters for evaluating model steerability and using LLMs as simulated respondents.

The experiments cover seven models, two questionnaires, and multiple persona samples. The item-level distributions and dimension summaries provide useful descriptive evidence of concentrated responses, especially for Harm and Fairness.

The distinction between relatively stable dimensions and more responsive dimensions is informative. The religion–Tradition analysis offers a useful qualification to blanket claims of persona insensitivity, and the discussion appropriately distinguishes desirable safety consistency from potentially problematic cultural rigidity.

Prompt templates, model snapshot identifiers, access dates, and extensive appendices support inspection. The limitations acknowledge simplified personas, single-turn evaluation, parser risks, and uncertain generalization to real interactions.
weaknesses: The central inference does not adequately distinguish aggregate stability from resistance to persona conditioning. Independent samples from the same persona generator can produce nearly identical averages even when individual attributes strongly affect responses. Pooled entropy and baseline-versus-persona-mixture JSD can also conceal opposing subgroup shifts. Increasing sample size establishes more stable estimates, not necessarily persona insensitivity. Repeated sampling of identical prompts and conditional analyses with uncertainty are needed to separate decoding variation from persona effects.

The robustness controls do not establish independence from elicitation format. Comparing persona and no-persona conditions while retaining forced choice does not test forced-choice artifacts. Section 3.6 also alternates between item ordering and response-option ordering, which are different interventions. Furthermore, the five dimension scores in Table 5 yield Pearson r approximately 0.487, whereas the text reports 0.77. Harm changes from 0.5967 to 0.1371, making the characterization of changes as minor questionable. Specify the tested model, randomization procedure, and correlation unit, and reconcile the numerical discrepancy.

The claimed universal steerability ordering is contradicted by Appendix J. In Table 10, Claude 3 Sonnet has higher JSD for Fairness than Ingroup (0.347 versus 0.225), and GPT-3.5 Turbo has higher JSD for Fairness than Purity (0.478 versus 0.326). Table 10 also omits LLaMA 3 8B. Separately, Table 6 lacks the third-seed Claude 3 Opus MFQ results despite the three-run summary in Table 4. These inconsistencies weaken the asserted robustness across every model and seed.

The selective-permeability analysis reports maximum pairwise Cohen’s d across demographic categories without group counts, confidence intervals, or model-specific estimates. Pooling three models and selecting the largest contrast leaves the precision and consistency of the reported effects unclear. This subset also includes Command-R+, outside the main seven-model experiment. Report uncertainty that accounts for repeated items/personas and establish whether the effects hold within individual models.

Parser validation does not adequately cover the experimental conditions. The human audit concerns only 89 no-persona responses from Claude 3 Haiku; the approximately 800-item parser comparison lacks sufficiently reported ground-truth validation. This does not establish accuracy across role-play responses from all evaluated models. Figure 11 also shows item totals below 200 without explaining the missing observations. Report refusal, invalid-output, and exclusion rates, and audit whether parsing or missingness affects concentration and demographic contrasts.

Reproducibility remains incomplete despite the useful documentation. The artifact link is deferred to the camera-ready version; baseline sample counts, the parser prompt, and explicit decoding settings are absent. MRAT centering and questionnaire-to-dimension mappings need precise specification, and the MFQ response anchors differ between Table 2 and Appendix B. Claims about intrinsic values, training origins, and general steering insufficiency also exceed what this single-template behavioral study establishes. These important but addressable methodological and reporting issues motivate resubmission next cycle.
